items.title: Repeated-recovery attribution rule is ambiguous about cumulative invalidation sets
items.reason: Every historical recovery writer (81eddb4, a15d7b9, implementation-recovery.ts:412-418) computes invalidatedContextIds/invalidatedObservationIds cumulatively over all prior affected-phase evidence. The verification record frames the check per between-recovery segment and says an extra id fails closed, so one reading fails closed on valid repeated same-frontier recoveries.
items.failure: The Phase 1 fold, implemented from the segment-scoped wording, rejects a second recovery at the same frontier because its set repeats ids already invalidated by the first recovery. A valid legacy run then reports fail-closed diagnostics.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Edit the Budget-stream evidence bullet in phase-0-verification.md to state cumulative prefix equality, matching implementation-recovery.ts:412-418.
items.mechanicalExplanation: Restate the rule as exact equality with the cumulative set the recovery writer computes: in the budget prefix before recovery R, all binding contexts and all observations on phases at or after R frontier, ordered by the predecessor authorized bytes. Extra means an id outside that set.

result_json.summary: Phase 0 is a verification-only phase with no product code. The commit records the integrated commit, reader inventory, gate identity ruling, legacy codec and keys, causal attribution algorithm, upgrade discovery, mutation boundary and codec fit. The claims checked against the 4af6e20 tree hold, and the recovery regression tests pass. One P2 wording correction: the repeated-recovery attribution rule must be stated as cumulative prefix equality so the Phase 1 fold does not fail closed on valid repeated same-frontier recoveries.

result_json.message: review: plan 215 phase 1 revision records and effective fold

items.title: Effective finding register marks addressed findings as pending
items.reason: foldEffectiveExecution lists every item of every observation as pending unless amendment-resolved, ignoring later priorFindings outcomes and repeating ids per round; Decision 6 requires one canonical register of unresolved findings.
items.failure: Completed plan-210 run run_bf10663c0a8a folds to 21 pending findings including closed ones and a duplicate 9/P2.2; a probe with R1 raised then priorFindings R1 addressed still returns R1 pending. Phase 3 carry would re-carry fixed findings.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Reuse the openCodeFindings semantics per phase in the fold's findings loop and add a multi-round test.

introducedBy.explanation: This hunk publishes foldEffectiveExecution as the store effective-revision reader. The returned register comes from the final findings loop in the same-range new-file hunk implementation-amendment.ts @@ -0,0 +1,1296 @@ (a single 1296-line hunk), which marks every observed item pending without consulting later priorFindings outcomes.

items.mechanicalExplanation: Per phase, derive the open set from the latest observation using the openCodeFindings rule in implementation.ts (latest items plus still_open/partially_addressed priorFindings, minus addressed), keep original identities once, then apply amendment resolutions.

items.title: Protected-section edit makes earlier-phase preservation impossible
items.reason: The fold rejects any amendment with preserved phases when Design Decisions/Acceptance/Scope/Not In Scope text changed; Decision 3 requires reviewer assessment of such out-of-section changes, not mechanical rejection.
items.failure: A probe changing one Design Decisions sentence and a Phase 2 item with Phase 1 preserved fails closed; every realistic semantic amendment (including the Player Desk acceptance with unchanged Phase 1) must reopen all phases, and a registered amendment could brick the run on read.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Remove the protectedText gate and add a positive test for a Design Decisions edit with Phase 1 preserved.

introducedBy.explanation: This hunk publishes foldEffectiveExecution as the store effective-revision reader, so its result fails closed for any amendment whose protected sections changed. The protectedText rejection itself is in the same-range new-file hunk implementation-amendment.ts @@ -0,0 +1,1296 @@ (a single 1296-line hunk).

items.mechanicalExplanation: Delete the protectedText comparison; preservation rests on phase-section, linked work-item and claim checks plus the reviewed preservedPhases reasons.

items.title: Linked work-item contracts not compared for preserved phases
items.reason: claimContract compares only debt-claim rows targeting the phase; Decision 3 also requires linked work-item contracts to be unchanged.
items.failure: A probe preserving '## Phase 1: Foundation (W1)' while W1's row changes from 2/0 to 8/3 with new rationale folds ok.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Extend the preserved-phase check to linked work-item ledger rows and add a negative test.
items.mechanicalExplanation: Also compare ledger rows for work-item ids named in the preserved phase heading/section.

items.title: Fold does not cross-check consumed amendmentScope
items.reason: The fold only requires amendmentScope to exist on the consumed authorization; durable records outside that scope are accepted as authority.
items.failure: A probe consuming a decision scoped to predecessor 'some-other-revision' and floor phase 3 for an amendment from binding-1 at boundary 2 folds ok.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Add the four scope checks at authorization consumption with negative tests.
items.mechanicalExplanation: On consumption, require scope.predecessorRevisionId equal, boundary not earlier than scope.earliestAffectedPhase in plan order, claimEdits subset of scope.claimEdits, and resolvedFindings subset of scope.resolutionRefs.

items.title: Corrections/credits citing invalidated observations stay applicable
items.reason: Correction attempts and credit reconciliations citing an invalidated observation keep applicability 'applicable' (certifies false), while decisions citing it become 'invalidated'.
items.failure: Phase 3 consumers reading applicability would treat an old correction shortcut on a reopened phase as carried evidence.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Mirror the decision-branch invalidation for correction and credit evidence and add a test.
items.mechanicalExplanation: Set applicability to invalidated when the cited observation is in the invalidated set, matching the decision branch.

items.title: Semantic amendment codec accepts duplicate list entries
items.reason: decodeImplementationSemanticAmendmentPayload does not reject repeated preservedPhases, resolvedFindings, or claimEdits entries, unlike parseAmendmentAssessment.
items.failure: A durable amendment repeating a preserved phase or resolved finding decodes and folds ok because the fold compares sets.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Reject duplicates in the decoder and add a codec test.

introducedBy.explanation: The new strict decoder maps the three lists without duplicate checks.

items.mechanicalExplanation: Apply the same duplicate-key checks used by parseAmendmentAssessment in the strict decoder.

items.title: Help tells reviewers to copy a plan diff into the assessment
items.reason: amendmentAssessment has no diff field; the help says to copy predecessor, hash, and plan diff.
items.failure: Reviewer agents may attempt to add an unknown diff key, which the strict parser rejects.

items.title: Missing negative tests and self-referential historical hash test
items.reason: No tests cover preserved-phase section change beyond checkboxes or changed linked claim contracts; the historical-hash test recomputes the expected value with the same function instead of pinning a pre-change hash.

items.lowestCostCorrection: Add the tests alongside the existing corrupt-lineage cases.

result_json.summary: Phase 1 codecs, protocol contract, and lineage verification are solid and keep historical runs compatible, but the effective finding register reports addressed findings as pending and the fold forbids preserving earlier phases whenever a shared design or scope section changes, contrary to Decisions 3 and 6. Both P1 fixes are mechanical; six P2 hardening and test items remain.
